say: You give it a line $l$ and a point $P$ that is **not** on $l$. It draws the line through $P$ that meets $l$ at a right angle.
The key idea: two points on $l$ that are the same distance from $P$ are found by one arc. Any point the same distance from both of them lies on the perpendicular through $P$.

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ above it. Construct the line through $P$ perpendicular to $l$.

steps.title: Cut the line twice
steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. Open it wider than the distance from $P$ to $l$. Draw an arc that cuts $l$ in two places. Call them $A$ and $B$.

lines.text: Now $|PA| = |PB|$, because both are the radius of the same arc.

steps.title: Cross two arcs
steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc below $l$. Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw a second arc that crosses the first. Call the crossing $Q$.

lines.text: Any setting works, as long as the two arcs cross.

steps.title: Join the points
steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line from $P$ to $Q$.

lines.text: Leave every arc on the page. They are the construction lines.

say: You give it a line $l$ and a point $P$ not on $l$. It draws the line through $P$ that is **parallel** to $l$.
The key idea: copy an angle. If a line through $P$ makes the same angle with a transversal as $l$ does, the two lines are parallel (corresponding angles are equal).

how.higher: It appeared once, on Paper 2 in 2015, as the construction step inside a 5-mark part where a proof is set out (given, diagram, construction, proof).

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ above it. Construct the line through $P$ parallel to $l$.

steps.title: Draw a transversal
steps.say: Pick a point $A$ on $l$. With the ruler, draw a line through $A$ and $P$, and extend it beyond $P$.

lines.text: This line crosses $l$ and passes through $P$.

steps.title: Mark the angle at A
steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$ and draw an arc that cuts $l$ at $B$ and the transversal at $C$.

lines.text: Do not change the compass setting.

steps.title: Copy the arc at P
steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. With the same setting, draw an arc that cuts the transversal at $D$. Measure the distance $|BC|$ with the compass.

lines.text: Then, with the point on $D$, mark that distance on the arc to find $E$, on the same side as $B$.

steps.title: Draw the parallel
steps.say: With the ruler, draw a line through $P$ and $E$.

lines.text: The angle at $P$ equals the angle at $A$. They are corresponding angles, so $PE \parallel l$.

higher.tip: Marks are given for a construction attempt, even if it is not complete, so always show your arcs and describe what you did.

say: You give it the length of the hypotenuse and the length of one other side. It draws the right-angled triangle.
The key idea: the hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. So draw the known side, make a right angle at its end, and swing an arc of the hypotenuse length from the other end.

example.question: Construct a right-angled triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 4$ cm, a right angle at $B$, and hypotenuse $|AC| = 7$ cm.

steps.title: Draw the known side
steps.say: With the ruler, draw a line segment $AB$ that is $4$ cm long.

steps.title: Make the right angle
steps.say: At $B$, construct the perpendicular to $AB$. Put the compass point on $B$ and cut $AB$ on both sides. Then draw two arcs of equal setting from those points so they cross above $B$. Draw a long line from $B$ through the crossing.

lines.text: You can use a set square here instead, but arcs show the method.

steps.title: Swing the hypotenuse
steps.say: Set the compass to $7$ cm on the ruler. Put the point on $A$ and draw an arc that cuts the perpendicular. Call the crossing $C$.

lines.text: The hypotenuse $AC$ is the longest side, so $C$ lies above $B$.
Check that $|AC| = 7$ cm and the angle at $B$ is $90^\circ$.

say: You give it one side and one acute angle of a right-angled triangle. It draws the triangle.
The key idea: you build two lines from the ends of the known side, one at the given angle and one at $90^\circ$. The triangle is closed where they meet.
what.in: one side and an acute angle

example.question: Construct a right-angled triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 5$ cm, a right angle at $B$, and $\angle A = 50^\circ$.

steps.title: Draw the known side
steps.say: With the ruler, draw a line segment $AB$ that is $5$ cm long.

steps.title: Measure the angle at A
steps.say: Put the centre of the protractor on $A$ with its base along $AB$. Mark $50^\circ$, then draw a long line from $A$ through the mark.

lines.text: Read from the zero that lies on $AB$.

steps.title: Make the right angle at B
steps.say: At $B$, construct the perpendicular to $AB$ with compass arcs. Draw a long line upward from $B$.

lines.text: You can use a set square here instead, but arcs show the method.

steps.title: Mark the third point
steps.say: The two long lines cross. Call the crossing $C$.
